holidays.name: National Buy a Musical Instrument Day
holidays.description: A day for treating yourself to a trumpet, ukulele, or kazoo and finally living out your rock star dreams. No talent required, only enthusiasm and tolerant neighbors.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance promoted by music retailers and enthusiasts to encourage people to take up music. Its exact founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Studies suggest that learning an instrument as an adult can boost memory and reduce stress, so your kazoo purchase is basically self-care.

holidays.name: World Goth Day
holidays.description: A day when fans of goth culture proudly show off their black clothing, dramatic eyeliner, and moody playlists, preferably under a cloudy sky.
holidays.origin: It began in the UK in 2009, started by DJs and event organizers from the goth scene including Cruel Britannia, to celebrate the subculture and its music.
holidays.funFact: Goth culture grew out of the late 1970s British post-punk scene, with Bauhaus's 1979 single 'Bela Lugosi's Dead' often called the first goth rock record.

holidays.name: National Vanilla Pudding Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the creamy, comforting dessert that gets overshadowed by chocolate. Grab a spoon and dig in, with or without a sliced banana.
holidays.origin: This is a food-calendar observance, with no known official founder, created to honor the classic dessert.
holidays.funFact: Banana pudding with vanilla wafers became a Southern staple after Nabisco began printing a recipe on its vanilla wafer boxes in the early 20th century.

holidays.name: Sherlock Holmes Day
holidays.description: Fans of the famous detective break out deerstalker hats, magnifying glasses, and dramatic deductions to honor his creator, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.
holidays.origin: May 22 is the birthday of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, born in Edinburgh, Scotland in 1859, so fans and Holmes societies celebrate the creator and his sleuth.
holidays.funFact: Sherlock Holmes never actually says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in any of Conan Doyle's original stories; the phrase came later from adaptations.

holidays.name: International Day for Biological Diversity
holidays.description: A United Nations day that celebrates all the wonderful weirdos of the natural world, from blobfish to bacteria, and reminds us why every species matters.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly proclaimed the day to raise awareness about biodiversity. It marks the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity text on May 22, 1992.
holidays.funFact: Scientists have described roughly 2 million species, but estimates of how many exist on Earth range into the many millions, so most are still unnamed.
